title: A Table for Mr. Costa
author: Lantern Original
summaryTr: Deniz kırmızı atkısını takıp ilk görüşmesine gider ve lüks bir restoranda yanlış kişi sanılır. Garsonlar titrer, şef gözyaşlarını güçlükle tutar, asıl sürpriz ise masanın yanında bekliyordur.
paragraphs: Deniz had two rules for his blind date: wear the red scarf, and don't be boring.

His friend Cem had arranged everything. "Her name is Mariana," Cem had said. "She wears a green coat, she loves food, and she's very funny. She'll know you by the scarf. The table is booked in her name. Costa. Just say Costa."

So at ten to eight, Deniz walked into Casa Lumi, the fanciest restaurant in town, with a red scarf around his neck and his heart beating fast. A man in a black suit stood by the door. His name tag said LUCA, MANAGER.

What Deniz did not know was that Luca had heard a rumour that morning. The famous food critic would visit Casa Lumi tonight. He was the man who could close a restaurant with one bad review. Nobody had ever seen his face. The newspaper printed only his name: M. Costa.
"Good evening," said Deniz. "I'm here for the Costa table."
Luca stopped moving. "The Costa table," he said slowly. "Of course. Mr. Costa. Welcome to Casa Lumi."
"No, I'm not—"
"Say no more." Luca put a finger on his lips and winked. "You wish to stay unknown. Your secret is safe with us."

Two minutes later, Deniz had the best table in the room, a glass of champagne that he had not ordered, and three waiters who were afraid to blink. "I think there's been a small mistake," he told the youngest one, a boy called Tomasz.
"There are no mistakes at Casa Lumi, sir," said Tomasz. His smile was shaking. "Only small surprises."
Deniz took out his phone to send Mariana a message. At once, the waiters froze.
"He's making notes," Tomasz whispered. "He's writing the review!"
"Nobody breathe," whispered Luca.

Then the food began to arrive. First came a soup with a tiny piece of gold on top. Then a fish, "caught this morning by the chef's uncle". Then a second soup, because the first one had only been "a small hello". Deniz was too polite to stop them, so he ate everything. At last the chef himself came out of the kitchen. Gaspard was a huge man with shaking hands. Behind him, twelve cooks watched through the little window in the kitchen door.
"Mr. Costa," the chef whispered. "How is the soup?"
Deniz looked at the gold, the cream and the faces at the window. He did not understand why the chef was nearly crying, but he wanted to say something kind. "It's... interesting," he said.
Gaspard turned white. From the kitchen came a small sound: twelve cooks saying "Interesting?" at the same moment.
"Interesting," the chef repeated. "Tomasz, is interesting good?"
"I don't know, Chef! It isn't excellent!"

Deniz was trying to think of a way to escape when the front door opened and a woman in a green coat came in. Dark hair, big smile, no scarf. Mariana! He jumped up and waved both arms, and Luca crossed the room like a goalkeeper.
"Good evening, madam. Do you have a booking?"
"Yes," said the woman. "Under Costa."

Luca narrowed his eyes. Another Costa? On this of all nights? This woman was clearly a fan who wanted to get close to the great critic. "I am so sorry," he said. "Mr. Costa is already here. But we do have a small table by the kitchen."

The woman looked across the room: the red scarf, the champagne, the three waiters, the chef who was almost crying. One of her eyebrows went up. "I see," she said slowly. "A small table would be perfect."

The small table was next to the toilets. Her bread was hard. Her soup was cold. The waiters did not look at her once, because they were too busy looking at Deniz. The woman took out a pen and began to write on a napkin. She looked as happy as a cat.

Deniz tried to go to her, but every time he stood up, a waiter appeared. "More fish, Mr. Costa?" "The chef has made a surprise for you, Mr. Costa!" At last he said, "Excuse me. I need the toilet." Nobody can say no to that. He walked past the toilet door and sat down at the small table next to it.
"Hello," he said. "I'm Deniz. I'm very sorry. I'm not Mr. Costa. I don't know why they think I am."
"I know," said the woman. "I'm Mariana Costa."
"Costa? But that's the booking name! So you're... you're..." He stopped.

"M. Costa, food writer at the Evening Post," she said. "Five years, and nobody has ever recognized me. Tonight they gave the critic's table to somebody else." She looked at the waiters, who were watching them from every corner like people watching a house on fire. "For five years, every restaurant has given me its best food. Tonight I'm eating like a normal person. It's wonderful. It's also terrible."
Deniz laughed so loudly that Luca dropped his clipboard.
"So what do we do now?" he asked.
"We eat," said Mariana. "You have seven dishes coming. I have a cold soup. Let's share."
Behind them, Tomasz pulled Luca's sleeve. "Look," he whispered. "Mr. Costa is eating the hard bread."
"What?" Luca went pale. "Why is he eating the bad bread?"
"It's a test! He's testing us!"

That was the end of the evening as Luca knew it. Within a minute, the best food in Casa Lumi was running across the restaurant to the table next to the toilets. Hot soup. The fish. The champagne. A cake with a candle on it. The twelve cooks left their places and stood in a line, hoping for one more "interesting". The woman in the green coat ate everything, wrote on three napkins, and did not stop smiling.
On Sunday, the Evening Post printed a review. It was short.

CASA LUMI. One star. The food is good, but the staff only see the person they expect to see. My soup was cold. My bread was older than the chef. The man in the red scarf received everything else, and he described it all as "interesting". He was right. — M. Costa
Gaspard put the review in a golden frame. Under the words "One star", he wrote one more word in red pen: INTERESTING.
Cem phoned Deniz on Monday morning. "Well? Did she recognize you by the scarf?"
"Cem," said Deniz, "everybody recognized me by the scarf."
Now Deniz and Mariana eat at Casa Lumi every Friday. They always ask for the table next to the toilets. Luca says it is the only table in the restaurant with a waiting list.

quiz.q: Why does Luca think Deniz is Mr. Costa?
options: Deniz says he is here for the Costa table
Deniz asks to speak to the chef
quiz.explainTr: Deniz 'Costa masası için geldim' der; Luca onu gizli kalmaya çalışan eleştirmen sanar.

quiz.q: What does Deniz say about the soup?
quiz.explainTr: Deniz kibarca 'interesting' der; şef ve aşçılar bu kelimenin iyi mi kötü mü olduğunu anlayamaz.

quiz.q: Why does Mariana sit at the small table by the toilets?
options: She does not like the other tables
Luca thinks she is a fan who wants to meet the critic
She arrives too late for a better table
quiz.explainTr: Luca, Mariana'yı ünlü eleştirmenle tanışmaya çalışan bir hayran sanır ve onu tuvaletin yanındaki masaya oturtur.

quiz.q: Who is the real food critic?
quiz.explainTr: M. Costa aslında Mariana Costa'dır; kimse onun yüzünü tanımıyordur.

quiz.q: Why do the waiters think Deniz is eating the hard bread?
options: He does not like the soft bread
quiz.explainTr: Garsonlar, 'Mr. Costa' sandıkları Deniz'in sert ekmeği yemesini restoranı test etmesi olarak yorumlar.
